hints: Look past the long carbon backbone and focus on the side chain, what functional group does $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ represent?
Remember that $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a methyl ester group, $-\text{COOCH}_3$, so think about the two classic hydrolysis conditions for esters.
Check if there is any $\text{O-H}$ bond in the polymer for sodium to attack, and then combine which of 1 and 2 work to pick the matching combination.
walkthrough:
**Spot the key functional group**

Look carefully at the repeating unit. The backbone is just C-C single bonds from addition polymerisation.

The reactive part is the side chain:
$$-\text{C(=O)OCH}_3$$

**Recognise it as an ester**

$-\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is just another way to write $-\text{COOCH}_3$, a methyl ester.

This is like Perspex, poly(methyl methacrylate). Esters undergo hydrolysis in both acid and alkali.

**Apply ester hydrolysis reactions**

With dilute aqueous acid, heated, acid hydrolysis gives carboxylic acid + alcohol:
$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

With aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, heated, base hydrolysis gives carboxylate salt + alcohol:
$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{R'OH}$$

So both 1 and 2 react with polymer X.

**Test sodium metal**

Sodium reacts with labile protons in $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{COOH}$ groups to give $\text{H}_2$.

Polymer X has only ester groups and alkyl C-H bonds, with no $\text{O-H}$ bonds at all. So sodium does nothing. Statement 3 is false.

Therefore only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This combination includes 1, 2 and 3. While 1 and 2 are correct for ester hydrolysis, 3 is wrong because sodium needs an acidic $\text{O-H}$ proton from an alcohol or carboxylic acid, which polymer X does not have.
options.B: Correct. This is 1 and 2 only. Aqueous sulfuric acid gives acid hydrolysis of the methyl ester side chains to $-\text{COOH}$ plus methanol, and aqueous sodium hydroxide gives base hydrolysis to $-\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ plus methanol. Sodium does not react.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes 2 and 3 only. It correctly includes base hydrolysis but wrongly includes sodium and wrongly leaves out acid hydrolysis. Esters are hydrolysed by both aqueous acid and aqueous alkali.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 1 only. It correctly includes acid hydrolysis but wrongly leaves out base hydrolysis. Students choosing this often forget that esters undergo saponification with $\text{NaOH}$ as well as acid hydrolysis.
